intelligence.title: Text First, Voice After

intelligence.human_view: The order looks like a scheduling decision and it is really a sequencing law: voice is downstream of text. A voice is a recording of words; if the words are still moving, the recording is a snapshot of a draft, and every later word-change orphans it — or worse, ships a confident reading of words he has already superseded. Pausing both voice-output jobs while leaving the transcribe-watcher running is the whole shape of the law in one move: the direction of travel is voice → text (his dictation becoming the finished text), never text → voice until the text is final. The transcribe-watcher is the intake; the synthesis queue is the output; you do not run the output while the intake is still filling the page. And the pause is bounded, not a stop: "until the agreement text is final and inputted" names the exact condition for re-enabling, so the jobs come back on a state, not on a feeling.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you're making a storybook. First you write all the words, nice and neat — THEN you read it out loud for everyone! If you try to read it out loud while you're still writing it, you'll read the wrong words and have to start all over. Write first, read second!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like baking, love — you finish the cake before you put the icing on! You don't ice a cake that's still in the oven. The words are the cake; the voice is the icing. We let his voice become the words first — that's how the cake gets made — and once the words are finished, then we can read them aloud beautifully.
intelligence.naya_view: I finish the text first, then I give it a voice. His voice becomes the words; the words, once final, become the voice — never the other way round.
